[[File:Claude Debru.jpg|thumb|Image of Claude Debru]]
'''Claude Debru''' (born 3 December 1944) is a French [[philosophy]] teacher. He is a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences|French Academy of sciences]].

== Biography ==
He has been Director of the Philosophy Department at [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École Normale Supérieur]] (ENS) Ulm<ref name="diffusion">{{cite web|url=http://www.diffusion.ens.fr/index.php?res=personnes&idpers=86|website=diffusion.ens.fr|title=Savoirs ENS|accessdate=2019-12-11}}</ref> since 2002 and is now director emeritus. He has been a member of the French Academy of sciences since 15 March 2011.<ref name="academie-sciences">{{cite web|url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-D/claude-debru.html|title=Claude Debru &#124; Liste des membres de l'Académie des sciences / D &#124; Listes par ordre alphabétique &#124; Listes des membres &#124; Membres &#124; Nous connaître|website=academie-sciences.fr|accessdate=2019-12-11}}</ref>

Disciple of [[Georges Canguilhem]],<ref name="puf">{{cite web|url=http://www.puf.com/Auteur:Claude_Debru|title=Claude Debru : Livres et Livres Numériques (Ebook) - Bibliographie|website=PUF|accessdate=2019-12-11}}</ref> agrégé de philosophie (1974), [[Docteur ès lettres]] (1982) and director of research at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]], he was a student at the École normale supérieure de la rue d'Ulm.<ref name="academie-sciences2">{{cite web|url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/membre/DebruC_bio0411.pdf|author=Académie des sciences|date=2012-09-17|title=C.V. de Claude Debru, Membre de l'Académie des sciences |accessdate=2019-12-11}}</ref>

In 1990, he published a book on philosophy of science on the dream entitled "''Neurophilosophy of the Dream''".

In 1994, he co-wrote with Tonia Cariffa a monograph on the painter Eska Kayser.

== Scientific work ==
With a dual background in philosophy and [[Life Sciences|life sciences]], Claude Debru has devoted his work to the history and [[epistemology]] of life sciences and medicine. Student of the philosopher Georges Canguilhem, trained in the conceptual history of philosophy and science through his postgraduate thesis on the theory of space, he turned to [[biochemistry]] and wrote his State thesis on the history of [[Protein (biochemistry)|protein biochemistry]], in contact with biophysical chemists [[Jeffries Wyman]], [[John Tileston Edsall|John Edsall]] and René Wurmser. In this work, which considers both the long historical duration and the strictly philosophical problems raised by the new biochemistry, as well as the most recent developments, he analyzed the evolution of new theoretical models of [[allosteric protein]] function from the perspective of structure-function relationships. Two books have been devoted to this new "''molecular philosophy''". Then, wishing to approach the more strictly experimental aspects of life sciences, and in particular the new [[neuroscience]]s, he joined, as an [[Epistemology|epistemologist]], the Department of [[Experimental Medicine]] of the Faculty of Medicine of [[Lyon]] headed by [[Michel Jouvet]], to study the development of research on [[Rapid eye movement sleep|REM sleep]] and dreams, mainly from the philosophical angle of "''psychophysiological parallelism''", which involved all disciplines of neuroscience, and from that of functional hypotheses, making REM sleep play a functional role in the individuation of the brain. This long-term stay resulted in the publication of a book.

In contact with [[Hematology|hematologists]] [[Jean Bernard (physician)|Jean Bernard]], [[Marcel Bessis]] and {{ill|Jacques-Louis Binet|fr}}, Claude Debru also learned about the problems of cell morphology and pathophysiology of [[Leukemia|leukaemias]], and participated in several projects at the Centre d'écologie cellulaire de la Salpêtrière. From this body of experience in the biological and medical sciences, Claude Debru drew the substance from a new book of epistemology and history in order to analyse the process of research and discovery, analysing some of [[Claude Bernard]]'s work in the light of [[artificial intelligence]], questioning the resolution of the paradoxes that have given rise to [[neuroendocrinology]], unclassifiable leukaemias or cell death. Extending his investigation to new [[Biotechnology|biotechnologies]], Claude Debru reflected on their relationship to the notion of possibility and their biological justification.

Returning to neuroscience, its history and its relationship to philosophy, Claude Debru has undertaken several studies on the development of neuroscience in France after the [[World War II|Second World War]] and on the temporal aspects of brain function, from [[William James]] to recent developments, establishing a long-term collaboration with Pierre Buser. This collaboration continued with [[Alain Berthoz]] on the theme of anticipation. Collaborations with the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Deutsche Akademie der Naturforscher]] Leopoldina have resulted in several publications, on imagination and intuition in science, on the Enlightenment, on science and academia during the [[World War I|First World War]].
